finding: In a cohort of HIV-infected pregnant women, maternal morbidity was more common following non-elective cesarean compared to elective cesarean or vaginal delivery, while HIV mother-to-child transmission rates did not differ by delivery mode.
mod_finding: HIV interruption as a cesarean indicator declined during the study, and maternal morbidity was more common following non-elective cesarean compared to elective cesarean or vaginal delivery, while HIV mother-to-child transmission rates did not differ by delivery mode.
